cards.front: How many copies of a static variable exist?
cards.back: One — even with many objects, or none at all
cards.extra: It belongs to the class, not to any instance, so every object reads and writes the same storage.
cards.source: freecodecamp.org — Java Static Keyword Explained With Examples
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: What are the four places static can be applied?
cards.extra: The same modifier with four different meanings: class-level state, class-level behaviour, class initialization and a nested type that needs no outer instance.
cards.source: freecodecamp.org — Java Static Keyword Explained With Examples
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: What two things can a static method never use?
cards.back: Non-static members, and the this or super keywords
cards.extra: There is no object when a static method runs, so there is no instance state to read and no current object to refer to.
cards.source: freecodecamp.org — Java Static Keyword Explained With Examples
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: In what order do static field initialisers and static blocks run?
cards.back: In source order, top to bottom, as one sequence
cards.extra: Text order matters: a static block that reads a field declared below it sees the default value, not the initialised one.
cards.source: freecodecamp.org — Java Static Keyword Explained With Examples
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::04 Static Keyword

cards.front: How do you instantiate a static nested class?
cards.extra: That is the difference from an inner class, which needs outer.new Inner(). The builder pattern's Builder class is the standard use.
